title: Humans or climate: who killed the megafauna?
summary: Giant animals vanished across continents in the Late Pleistocene. The weight of human versus climatic causes is long disputed, though most scholars accept at least some human role.
why: If humans did it, it was one of our species' first continent-wide impacts.

notes.problem: Source: 'most scholars support at least a contributory role of humans'; pure-climate theory overstated as an equal rival.

question: Were humans or climate change mainly responsible for the Ice Age megafauna extinctions?
evidence: Sahul losses from about 50,000 years ago; northern Eurasia staggered 50,000–10,000; North America concentrated 13,800–11,400 years BP.
wouldSettle: Precisely dated last appearances compared with human arrival and climate records, continent by continent.

theories.name: Human hunting and impact
theories.idea: Extinctions follow human arrival on each continent, suggesting people drove the losses.

theories.name: Climate change
theories.idea: Late Pleistocene climate shifts were the main driver; now a minority view as the sole cause.
